caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: DANDI:000045
attempts.entry_title: Standardized and reproducible decision-making in mice (The International Brain Laboratory 2021)
attempts.description: Tests the findings of The International Brain Laboratory (2021) on dandiset 000045, which holds the trial tables of 178 mice trained in seven laboratories from June 2019 to March 2020. It recomputes basic and full task proficiency from the trials and compares training times, psychometric parameters, block effects, the choice model and session ends with the paper, across laboratories. The dandiset holds no sessions before June 2019 and no training status.

notebooks.title: Reproducing The International Brain Laboratory (2021) from dandiset 000045

outcomes.statement: Of 206 mice that started training, 140 reached proficiency in the basic task and 98 in the full task.
outcomes.source: Results, opening section, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: Out of 206 mice that started training, 140 achieved proficiency in the basic task, and 98 in the full task
outcomes.notes: The dataset holds 177 mice of the paper's project; 136 have their whole training in it (first session a first-stage session), against 206 that started training. Under the main reading 83 reach basic task proficiency (61 first with status 1a, 22 with 1b), against 140; the pipeline's contrast check gives 85, and 1b replacing 1a from 2019-09-12 gives 70 and 71. 60 reach full task proficiency, against 98. No count is within tolerance under any reading. The answers of 2026-10-22 changed P1 (each session and the two before it, any protocol; all trials counted; percent correct over 50% and 100% contrasts; 1a or 1b at any date), which moved the count from 75 to 84 under the earlier readings to 83 under the main one; the outcome is the same as before (not_reproduced). The dataset holds sessions from 2019-06-11 to 2020-03-23; the Methods say training of these mice began in January 2019. No window fails the 1b or P2 criteria only because missing stimulus onsets leave its reaction time undefined (0 windows under every reading), so the missing onsets do not lower the counts. P2 slides over full-task days; 10 days with more than one full-task session fall at or before a mouse's P2 day, or on any day of a mouse without P2, in 7 mice, so a count over sessions could differ for at most 7 mice.
deviations: Proficiency is recomputed from the trials, as the files carry no training status.
P2 is computed over three consecutive full-task days, not sessions (see notes).
Mice whose first session in the dataset is not a first-stage session (41) are left out, as their training began before the dataset does.

outcomes.statement: Basic task training took 18.4 +- 13.0 days (s.d., n = 140 mice), from 3 days for the fastest mouse to 59 days for the slowest.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 2g
outcomes.quote: The average training took 18.4 ± 13.0 days (s.d., n = 140, Figure 2g )
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading (83 mice) the mean days to P1 is 19.87 counting the P1 day and 18.87 without, both within 18.4 +- 1.84, and the slowest mouse takes 58 and 57 days, within 59 +- 5.9. The s.d. is 11.39 (against 13.0 +- 1.3) and the fastest mouse takes 5 or 4 days (against 3 +- 0.3); two of four values are within tolerance. The variants give means of 17.73 to 23.17 days and at most two values within tolerance. Six of the 136 whole-training mice have their first session in the dataset's first 7 days, where an earlier start would go unseen; without the 2 of them that reach P1 the mean is 19.40 days (s.d. 10.98, fastest 5, slowest 58), again two of four within tolerance. The five fastest mice start between 2019-08-06 and 2019-11-21. The answers changed P1 (see cohort-counts); the outcome is the same as before (partially_reproduced). Measured is the main reading, counting the P1 day.
deviations: 83 mice, against 140.

outcomes.statement: The number of days to basic task proficiency differed across laboratories; within-lab interquartile ranges ranged from 8 days (Lab 2) to 22 days (Lab 6).
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 2g
outcomes.quote: The number of days needed to achieve basic task proficiency was different across laboratories ( Figure 2g , p<0.001, Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric test followed by a post-hoc Dunn's multiple comparisons test)

statistics.test: Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric test, then post-hoc Dunn's multiple comparisons test

outcomes.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across labs p = 0.029 under the main reading (0.023 to 0.088 under the variants), never below 0.001; the code's switch gives the same tests. Lab 2 interquartile range 7.75 days (within 8 +- 0.8), Lab 6 5.75 days (against 22 +- 2.2). The labs differ at p < 0.05 but not at the p < 0.001 the criterion requires, and one of the two ranges matches, so the effect is present but weaker. Changed from not_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, which gave partially_reproduced for this reason.
deviations: 6 to 26 mice per lab.

outcomes.statement: Measured in trials, basic task training took 10.8 +- 8.6 thousand trials (s.d., n = 140), from one thousand for the fastest mouse to 43 thousand for the slowest; reaching 80% correct on easy trials took on average about 7.4 thousand trials.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 2, figure supplement 1
outcomes.quote: For mice that learned the task, the average training took 10.8 ± 8.6 thousands of trials (s.d., n = 140) ... The fastest learner met training criteria in one thousand trials, the slowest 43 thousand trials. To reach 80% on easy trials took on average ~7.4 thousand trials.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading the mean trials to P1 is 11,839 counting the P1 day and 11,104 without, within 10,800 +- 1,080; the s.d. (7,515 and 7,472), fastest (2,357 and 1,687) and slowest (34,998 and 34,265) are outside tolerance. The mean cumulative trials when mean easy-trial performance first exceeds 80% is 7,329 (within 7,400 +- 740), and 6,659 to 7,306 under the variants. The answers changed P1; the outcome is the same as before (partially_reproduced).
deviations: The median filter over 3 sessions is pandas' centred rolling median with partial windows at the ends, a standard choice; the claims file does not fix the edges.

outcomes.statement: About 80% of mice that started training would learn the basic task within the 40 days usually allotted (Kaplan-Meier estimate over all 206 mice).
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 4; Figure 2h
outcomes.quote: there was a 80% probability that mice would learn the task within the 40 days that were usually allotted, and when mice were trained for a longer duration, the success rate rose even further ( Figure 2h )
outcomes.notes: Over the 136 mice that started training in the dataset, mice without P1 censored, the Kaplan-Meier proportion at day 40 is 0.749 counting the P1 day and 0.749 without under the main reading, within 0.8 +- 0.08, and 1.000 at the last day. Since round 1 a mouse without P1 is censored at its last training day counted the same way as the events (before, at the count including the P1 day under both counts), which moved the count without the P1 day from 0.741 to 0.749. The pipeline's contrast check, a variant, gives 0.768; 1b replacing 1a from 2019-09-12 gives 0.600 to 0.602, outside tolerance. The code's variant, leaving out mice still in training at the cutoff, gives 0.815 under the main reading. The answer to the question on "all contrasts introduced" (each of the three sessions, the main reading; the pipeline's check of the current session a variant; pooling given by neither) settled the reading that blocked the claim, and the change of P1 to the pipeline's computation moved the proportion under that reading from 0.670 to 0.678 to 0.741 to 0.749. Earlier outcome blocked (methods_underspecified).
deviations: Without status labels, time is the training days to P1 for proficient mice and the total training days otherwise, as the criterion says; mice without P1 are censored.
The variant takes "still in training at the cutoff" as a session in the last 7 days of the dataset, a choice for a variant that decides nothing.

outcomes.statement: Contrast threshold and bias varied little during training; the threshold interquartile range slightly decreased from 12-29% in the first 10 training days to 11-23% thereafter, and the bias interquartile range went from -5.2 to 7.1% to -5.6 to 6.5%.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 2b,c
outcomes.quote: Estimates of contrast threshold did not vary much during training ( Figure 2b ), with an interquartile range that slightly decreased from 12–29% during the first 10 training days, and 11–23% thereafter. Likewise, bias did not vary much, with an interquartile range of −5.2% to 7.1% during the first 10 days to −5.6% to 6.5% thereafter ( Figure 2c ).
outcomes.notes: Under every reading the threshold interquartile range narrows after day 10 (main, filtered, days 10 to 39, 11.5-23.7% against 11.1-24.3%), but no reading puts all eight bounds within tolerance; the main reading puts at most four (filtered, days 10 on). The answer on 50:50 sessions (the basic-task sessions with all their trials) confirms the sessions used; the change of P1 changed the mice. Earlier outcome the same (partially_reproduced). Measured is the main reading, filtered, days 10 to 39.
deviations: Fits are per training day, all sessions of the day pooled (1,427 days).

outcomes.statement: During training mice were not systematically biased to one side; absolute bias averaged 9.8 +- 12.1 (s.d.), and contrast threshold, which stabilized after about 10 sessions, averaged 17.8 +- 11.7%.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 2b,c
outcomes.quote: Mice across laboratories were not systematically biased towards a particular side and the absolute bias was similar across laboratories (9.8 ± 12.1 [s.d.] on average). Likewise, measures of contrast threshold stabilized after the first ~10 sessions, which was on average 17.8 ± 11.7% on average across institutions.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading both means are within tolerance under every reading pooled over sessions. Under the first reading listed (filtered, pooled) the absolute bias is 8.821 and the threshold after day 10 18.39%; without the filter 9.759 and 18.56%. The s.d.s are below the paper's under every reading (6.30 to 8.72 against 12.1; 8.55 to 9.89 against 11.7). The statement's "similar across laboratories" is not tested by the criterion; lab means of the signed bias run from -5.11 to 2.55 (main, filtered). The answers changed P1; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).

outcomes.statement: Variability in performance across mice decreased with training but did not disappear; between training days 15 and 40, mean easy-trial performance rose from 80.7% to 91.1% while its s.d. across mice fell from 19.1% to 10.1%.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 3; Figure 2, figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: For example, between training days 15 and 40, when the average performance on easy trials of the mice increased from 80.7% to 91.1%, the variation across mice (s.d.) of performance on easy trials decreased from 19.1% to 10.1%.
outcomes.notes: The mean rises and the s.d. falls between days 15 and 40 under every reading, and the means are within tolerance under every reading, but no reading has both s.d.s within tolerance (15.03 to 17.12% at day 15 against 19.1%; 6.86 to 12.19% at day 40 against 10.1%). The answers changed P1 and confirm the 50:50 sessions of reading (2); earlier outcome the same (partially_reproduced).
deviations: Reading (3) averages each mouse's days within the bin before taking the mean and s.d. over mice; the claims file does not say how the bin is pooled.

outcomes.statement: A Random Forests decoder applied to the change in easy-trial performance over the first five sessions predicted whether a mouse would be in the bottom quartile of learning speed with 53% accuracy (chance 25%), and misclassified a top-quartile mouse as bottom-quartile only 7% of the time.
outcomes.source: Results, Training succeeded but with different rates across mice and laboratories, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: A Random Forests decoder applied to change in performance (% correct with easy, high-contrast stimuli) in the first five sessions was able to predict whether a mouse would end up in the bottom quartile of learning speed (the slowest learners) with accuracy of 53% (where chance is 25%). Conversely, the chance of misclassifying a fast-learning, top quartile mouse as a slow-learning, bottom quartile mouse, was only 7%.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading of P1 the criterion's readings disagree on whether the accuracy is near 53%; 3 of 20 accuracy values are within 0.53 +- 0.053 (features (b), four quartiles from days, recall 0.571, four-class accuracy 0.518, precision 0.571), the others run from 0.143 to 0.667. Top-quartile mice classed as bottom quartile, 0.000 to 0.143. The answers changed P1 but not the readings that block the claim; earlier outcome the same. Measured is features (a), four quartiles from days, recall.
deviations: The Random Forest's seed is a standard choice (0).
The criterion's readings are run under the main reading of P1 only, to keep the notebook within its time limit.

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency, errors on easy (50% and 100%) contrasts were low, 9.5 +- 3.6%, with no significant difference across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 3c
outcomes.quote: The lapse rates (i.e., the errors made in response to easy contrasts of 50% and 100%) were low (9.5 ± 3.6%, Figure 3c ) with no significant difference across laboratories.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading easy-trial errors at proficiency are 8.41 +- 3.79% (81 mice); the s.d. is within tolerance, the mean just outside 9.5 +- 0.95. The pipeline's contrast check, a variant, gives 9.66 +- 3.69% (85 mice), both within tolerance; 1b replacing 1a gives 5.26 and 5.84%. Two of the 83 mice with P1 have no basic-task session in S1. The answers changed P1, and the main reading now decides; earlier outcome reproduced (8.56 +- 3.77% under 1a/each). The statement's "no significant difference across laboratories" is fig3cde-no-lab-difference-medians.

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency the contrast threshold was similar across laboratories at 14.3 +- 3.8 (s.d., n = 7 laboratories) and the response bias was small at 0.3 +- 8.4.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 3d,e
outcomes.quote: The slope of the curves, which measures contrast sensitivity, was also similar across laboratories, at 14.3 ± 3.8 (s.d., n = 7 laboratories, Figure 3d ). Finally, the horizontal displacement of the curve, which measures response bias, was small at 0.3 ± 8.4 (s.d., n = 7, Figure 3e ).
outcomes.notes: Over mice, under the main reading, threshold 14.09 +- 3.80 and bias -0.46 +- 8.09, all four within tolerance; also under the pipeline's contrast check (13.89 +- 3.92 and 0.16 +- 9.05). Over the seven lab means the s.d.s are 1.14 to 2.24. The answers changed P1; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency, easy-trial performance, contrast threshold and bias did not differ in median across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 3c-e
outcomes.quote: None of these measures showed a significant difference across laboratories, either in median (performance: p=0.63, threshold: p=0.81, bias: p=0.81, FDR corrected Kruskal-Wallis test)
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading the corrected Kruskal-Wallis p are 0.287 (performance), 0.439 (threshold) and 0.730 (bias), all >= 0.05; the code's switch to ANOVA gives the same. Lab medians, performance 89.0 to 93.1%, threshold 12.3 to 17.1, bias -6.1 to 1.8. The pipeline's contrast check gives the same outcome (smallest 0.395); with 1b replacing 1a from 2019-09-12, a variant, performance differs across labs (corrected p = 0.038 and 0.026). The answers removed the pooled reading of "all contrasts introduced" and made "1a or 1b at any date" the main reading, so the readings that disagreed no longer decide. Earlier outcome blocked (methods_underspecified).
deviations: 6 to 25 mice per lab.

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency, easy-trial performance, contrast threshold and bias did not differ in variance across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 1; Figure 3c-e
outcomes.quote: or in variance (performance: p=0.09, threshold: p=0.57, bias: p=0.57, FDR corrected Levene's test)
outcomes.notes: Corrected Levene p for performance, threshold and bias are 0.268, 0.268 and 0.299 under the main reading and all >= 0.05 under every variant (smallest 0.212). Lab s.d.s (main), performance 1.48 to 4.35, threshold 2.35 to 4.75, bias 4.66 to 10.57. The answers changed P1; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).
deviations: Trials per minute uses the session duration from the file's start and end times.

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency the median trial duration (stimulus onset to feedback) was 468 +- 221 ms, with some differences across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 4; Figure 3, figure supplement 2a
outcomes.quote: The median time from stimulus onset to feedback (trial duration, a coarse measure of reaction time) was 468 ± 221 ms, showing some differences across laboratories ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2a , p=0.004, Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric test)
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading the median trial duration is 420.45 ms, just below 468 +- 46.8, with s.d. 219 ms (within 221 +- 22.1). The Kruskal-Wallis test across labs gives p = 0.061 uncorrected (0.12 corrected), and 0.068 to 0.40 under the variants, so the difference across labs that the criterion requires (p < 0.05) is not found. Lab 4's median is 702 ms against 370 to 455 ms for the others. One of the two values is within tolerance and the other just outside, and the lab difference is not significant, so the claim holds in part. Changed from not_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, which gave partially_reproduced.
deviations: Trials without a stimulus onset time (6% of all trials) have no duration and are left out.

outcomes.statement: At basic task proficiency mice performed 719 +- 223 trials per session; the difference across laboratories was significant but only in one laboratory relative to the rest.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 4; Figure 3, figure supplement 2b
outcomes.quote: Mice on average performed 719 ± 223 trials per session ( Figure 3—figure supplement 2b ). This difference was significant (p<10 −6 , one-way ANOVA) but only in one laboratory relative to the rest.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading 706.8 trials per session (within 719 +- 71.9), s.d. 196.9 (outside 223 +- 22.3). One-way ANOVA p = 1.2e-04, below 0.05 and not below 1e-6; the five significant Tukey pairs all involve Lab 7 (412 trials per session against 635 to 836). The variants give p = 9.2e-05 to 0.0026, every pair with Lab 7. The answers changed P1; earlier outcome the same (partially_reproduced).

outcomes.statement: A Naive Bayes classifier could not identify a mouse's laboratory from its basic-task performance, threshold and bias; its accuracy was 0.12 +- 0.051 against a chance level of 0.11, and the 95% range of its distribution included chance.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 5; Figure 3f
outcomes.quote: Its mean accuracy was 0.12 ± 0.051, and a 95th percentile of its distribution included the chance level of 0.11 (mean of the null distribution).
outcomes.notes: The answer on the subsample size (the Methods' rule, the lowest lab count over the datasets classified, one size for every classifier claim) let the classifier run with 5 mice per lab (Lab 4 and Lab 7 in S2, Lab 7 in the first full-task sessions). Naive Bayes on S1 (81 mice) has accuracy 0.140 +- 0.063 (within 0.12 +- 0.051) against a shuffled mean of 0.106 (within 0.11 +- 0.011); its 2.5th percentile, 0.029, is below the shuffled mean, so it is not above chance. Under the pipeline's contrast check, 0.138, 2.5th percentile 0.029, null 0.110. The code's 8 mice per lab cannot run (Lab 4 and Lab 7 hold 7 and 6 mice in S1). Earlier outcome blocked (other, fewer than 8 mice in some labs).
deviations: 5 mice per lab, 35 per subsample, against 8 and 56 in the paper.
The leave-one-out Naive Bayes is computed directly; it agrees with scikit-learn's GaussianNB on every subsample checked (synthetic data and 20 subsamples of S1).

outcomes.statement: With the laboratory's time zone added as a feature, the classifier performed above chance and confused labs in the same time zone.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 5; Figure 3f; Figure 3, figure supplement 3b
outcomes.quote: If the classifier was given this variable during training and testing it performed above chance ( Figure 3f , Positive control ) and the confusion matrix showed clusters of labs located in the same time zone
outcomes.notes: With the time zone as a fourth feature and 5 mice per lab, accuracy 0.405 +- 0.084; the 2.5th percentile (0.257) and the code's 0.001th percentile (0.171) are above the shuffled mean of 0.118. In the mean confusion matrix all off-diagonal mass lies on labs in the same time zone (4.166 over 12 cells, against 0.000 over 30 cells of other zones); Lab 7, alone in its zone, is always classified correctly. The time zones come from the code (lab-link); the start times in the files cannot confirm them. The subsample answer let the claim run; earlier outcome blocked (other).
deviations: 5 mice per lab, as for fig3f-classifier-chance-basic.

outcomes.statement: Random Forest and Logistic Regression classifiers also failed to predict laboratory membership from basic-task behavior.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 5; Figure 3, figure supplement 3d-i
outcomes.quote: Similar results were obtained with two other classifier algorithms ( Figure 3—figure supplement 3d–i ).
outcomes.notes: With 5 mice per lab (answer of 2026-10-22), Logistic Regression is not above chance (accuracy 0.071 +- 0.054, 2.5th percentile 0.000, shuffled mean 0.070, 2000 subsamples). The Random Forest (100 trees, leave-one-out) now runs in 4 processes at 3.7 s per subsample, about 2 h for the 2000 subsamples of the criterion, so the first 50 of the same sequence are run; its accuracy is 0.130 +- 0.055, 2.5th percentile 0.035 (bootstrap 95% interval 0.029 to 0.057) against a shuffled mean of 0.100, so it is not above chance; the first 25 give the same (0.046 against 0.098). Earlier outcome blocked (not_runnable), with 6 subsamples; the verifier's round 1 noted the run time is not a data limit and asked for a larger run. Measured is the Random Forest's 2.5th percentile and shuffled mean.
deviations: The Random Forest is run on the first 50 of the 2000 subsamples, to keep the notebook within its time limit.

Logistic Regression with solver liblinear is fitted one-vs-rest, as scikit-learn did for several classes with this solver when the paper's code ran (the installed version refuses more than two classes); the direct Newton fit of liblinear's objective agrees with scikit-learn's OneVsRestClassifier on every subsample checked.

outcomes.statement: The institutions named in the dandiset's files are the paper's seven laboratories, so that the code's lab numbers (Lab 1 to 7) and time zones can be given to the dataset's mice.
outcomes.source: Claims file header, code lab numbers and time zones (paper-behavior at commit edc4531)
outcomes.notes: The 7 institutions in the files match the code's 7 labs one to one; CSHL holds churchlandlab and zadorlab, SWC hoferlab and mrsicflogellab. The start times do not bear out the time zones, as they are local clock times stated as UTC (median start hours 11.0 to 14.4 h in every lab, Lab 7 at 11.0 h). Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: In the basic task, mouse choices were no more consistent within laboratories than across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Figure 3, figure supplement 1a legend
outcomes.quote: This averaged consistency was not significantly higher (p=0.73) than a null distribution generated by randomly shuffling lab assignments between mice and computing the average within-lab choice variability 10,000 times ( violin plot ). Therefore, choices were no more consistent within labs than across labs.

statistics.test: permutation test against 10,000 shuffles of lab labels

outcomes.notes: Within-lab consistency is not above the shuffles (main reading p = 0.458 on S1 and 0.535 on the code's sessions; variants 0.440 to 0.861). The answers changed P1; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).
deviations: The code's sessions (P1 day and two after) take the basic-task trials and the 50:50 trials of full-task sessions on those days.

outcomes.statement: In the full task, neither choice fractions nor the bias shift between blocks were more consistent within laboratories than expected by chance.
outcomes.source: Figure 3, figure supplement 1b,c legend; Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 4
outcomes.quote: Within-lab choice consistency on the full task was not higher than expected by chance, p=0.25. ... Within-lab consistency in bias shift was not higher than expected by chance (p=0.31).

statistics.test: permutation test against 10,000 shuffles of lab labels
permutation test against 10,000 shuffles of lab labels

outcomes.notes: Choices per contrast and block are more consistent within labs than in shuffles (consistency 98.2 against a null mean of 82.5, p = 0.017, 60 mice). The bias shift is not (p = 0.154), as in the paper. Not affected by the answers (P2 is unchanged).
deviations: 60 mice, against 98; 5 to 21 per lab.

outcomes.statement: With a looser proficiency criterion (80% correct on easy trials over three sessions, n = 150 mice), behavior was again consistent across laboratories; only the number of trials per session differed slightly, and a classifier failed to identify a mouse's laboratory.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 6; Figure 3, figure supplement 4
outcomes.quote: there was a small but significant difference in the number of trials per session across laboratories. All other measured parameters were similar.
outcomes.notes: 91 mice meet the looser criterion (against 150 +- 15). Trials per session differ across labs (corrected p = 0.0022), and so do trials per minute (corrected p = 0.0022), against the criterion's other five >= 0.05. With the subsample answer the classifier now runs (5 mice per lab) and is not above chance (accuracy 0.117 +- 0.058, 2.5th percentile 0.029, shuffled mean 0.110), as the criterion requires. The other four lab tests give corrected p 0.078 to 0.92. One of the six lab tests differs from the criterion and the count is far below the paper's, so the claim holds in part. Changed from not_reproduced after the verifier's round 1, which gave partially_reproduced.

outcomes.statement: In the first three sessions of the full task, bias in each block, contrast threshold in each block and performance on 100% contrast trials did not vary significantly across laboratories, and a classifier could not predict lab membership.
outcomes.source: Figure 3, figure supplement 5 legend; Results, Performance in the basic task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 6
outcomes.quote: Bias for each block prior did not vary significantly over labs (Kruskal-Wallis test, 20:80 blocks; p=0.96, 50:50 block; p=0.96, 80:20 block; p=0.89). ( b ) The contrast thresholds also did not vary systematically over labs (Kruskal-Wallis test, 20:80 block; p=0.078, 50:50 block; p=0.12, 80:20 block; p=0.17). ( c ) Performance on 100% contrast trials neither (Kruskal-Wallis test, p=0.15).
outcomes.notes: On the legend's sessions from P1b, now the first full-task session at or after P1 by the answer of 2026-10-22 (72 mice), three of the seven Kruskal-Wallis p are below 0.05 (threshold in 20:80 blocks 0.022, in 50:50 blocks 0.038, performance on 100% contrast 0.022). Every variant also has a p below 0.05 (smallest 0.001 to 0.025; the code's P1b, 66 mice, 0.007). With the code's Holm-Sidak correction, a variant, the smallest is 0.141. The classifier now runs (5 mice per lab) and is not above chance (accuracy 0.170 +- 0.048, 2.5th percentile 0.086, shuffled mean 0.114). Earlier outcome the same (not_reproduced).

outcomes.statement: Mice incorporated the block priors into their choices from the first sessions of the full task.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 3, figure supplement 5a
outcomes.quote: Mice incorporated block priors into their choices already from the first sessions in which they were exposed to this full task
outcomes.notes: Bias is higher in 80:20 than in 20:80 blocks in the first full-task sessions under every reading (main, legend sessions, median difference 4.45, 69 of 72 mice, Wilcoxon p = 2.1e-13; all readings, median 4.35 to 6.40, p <= 2.0e-12), with P1b as the answer gives it and with the code's P1b. The variant against the proficiency threshold of 5 finds 30 of 73 to 39 of 66 mice above it. Earlier outcome the same (reproduced).

outcomes.statement: Mice that reached full task proficiency took 31.5 +- 16.1 days, or 20,494 +- 10,980 trials (s.d., n = 98), from the start of training; the fastest took 8 days (4691 trials), the slowest 81 days (61,316 trials).
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 2
outcomes.quote: For mice that reached full task proficiency, the average training from start to finish took 31.5 ± 16.1 days, or 20,494 ± 10,980 trials (s.d., n = 98). ... The fastest learner achieved proficiency in 8 days (4691 trials), the slowest 81 days (61,316 trials).
outcomes.notes: 60 mice reach P2 in 29.4 +- 14.1 days and 19,637 +- 9,173 trials; the means are within tolerance, the s.d.s and extremes are not (fastest 10 days and 5,592 trials, slowest 64 days and 43,500 trials, against 8, 4,691, 81 and 61,316). 30 mice without P2 still had sessions in the dataset's last week, which cuts off the slowest learners. Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: Block structure had the greatest effect on choices when sensory evidence was absent; the shift in rightward choices between 20:80 and 80:20 blocks was highest at 0% contrast in every laboratory, averaging 28.5%.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 4c-e
outcomes.quote: The average shift in rightward choices was invariably highest at 0% contrast, where rightward choices in the two blocks differed by an average of 28.5%.
outcomes.notes: Mean shift at 0% contrast 28.00% over 60 mice (within 28.5 +- 2.85); the lab mean is highest at 0% in all 7 labs (23.0 to 36.2%). Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: The bias shift at 0% contrast did not differ across laboratories more than within them.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 4d,e
outcomes.quote: This value did not significantly differ across laboratories any more than it differed within laboratories (one-way ANOVA F(6) = 1.345, p=0.2455, Figure 4d,e ).
outcomes.notes: One-way ANOVA across labs F = 2.07, p = 0.072 (paper F = 1.345, p = 0.2455); lab means 23.0 to 36.2%. Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: Block type did not significantly affect the contrast threshold.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 3; Figure 4f
outcomes.quote: Changes in block type did not significantly affect the contrast threshold (Wilcoxon Signed-Rank test, p=0.85, n = 98 mice, Figure 4f ).
outcomes.notes: Threshold 20:80 minus 80:20, median 0.08, 31 of 60 positive, Wilcoxon p = 0.80. Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: Block type changed lapse rates, which were higher on the left in 20:80 blocks and higher on the right in 80:20 blocks.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 3; Figure 4g,h
outcomes.quote: However, it did change the lapse rates, which were consistently higher on the left in the 20:80 blocks and on the right in the 80:20 blocks
outcomes.notes: Left lapse higher in 20:80 (median 0.015, 46 of 60, p = 2.3e-06) and right lapse higher in 80:20 (0.018, 45 of 60, p = 2.2e-05); the directions hold with p < 0.05 but not with p < 1e-6 and 1e-7. Not affected by the answers.
deviations: 60 mice, against 98.

outcomes.statement: Block type changed the overall bias consistently, with curves shifting left in 20:80 blocks and right in 80:20 blocks.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 3; Figure 4i
outcomes.quote: Finally, as expected there was a highly consistent change in overall bias, with curves shifting to the left in 20:80 trials and to the right in 80:20 trials
outcomes.notes: Bias higher in 80:20 than in 20:80 in all 60 mice (median 7.11, p = 1.6e-11). This is the smallest p a Wilcoxon test gives with 60 mice, so the paper's p < 1e-16 cannot be reached; the criterion gives partial. Not affected by the answers.
deviations: 60 mice, against 98.

outcomes.statement: Threshold, lapses and bias in each block type showed no significant differences across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 4f-i
outcomes.quote: An analysis of the psychometric curves showed highly consistent effects of block type, with no significant differences across laboratories ( Figure 4f–i ).
outcomes.notes: Corrected p for the eight per-block parameters 0.19 to 0.88 (code's test switch, FDR). Not affected by the answers.

outcomes.statement: A classifier trained on the full-task psychometric parameters could not predict the laboratory of individual mice above chance.
outcomes.source: Results, Performance in the full task was indistinguishable across laboratories, paragraph 3; Figure 4j
outcomes.quote: Just as in the basic task ( Figure 3 ), a classifier trained on these variables could not predict above chance the origin laboratory of individual mice above chance ( Figure 4j ).
outcomes.notes: With the subsample answer the classifier runs with 5 mice per lab. Naive Bayes on the eight per-block values of S2 (60 mice) has accuracy 0.176 +- 0.046; its 2.5th percentile (0.086) is below the shuffled mean of 0.107, so it is not above chance. The code's 8 mice per lab cannot run, as five labs hold fewer. Earlier outcome blocked (other).
deviations: 5 mice per lab, as for fig3f-classifier-chance-basic.

outcomes.statement: In a logistic choice model fitted to each mouse, visual weights grew with contrast to above 3 at 100% contrast, while weights for past choices were much smaller and positive after both rewarded (basic 0.19, full 0.42) and unrewarded (basic 0.33, full 0.46) trials, indicating perseverance.
outcomes.source: Results, A probabilistic model reveals common strategies across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 5c,d,f,g
outcomes.quote: As expected, visual terms had large weights, which grew with contrast to reach values above 3 at 100% contrast. Weights for non-sensory factors were much lower ( Figure 5c,f , note different scale). Weights for past choices were positive for both rewarded (basic 0.19, full 0.42) and unrewarded previous trials (basic 0.33, full 0.46)
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading of P1b the 100% weight is above 3 in both tasks (3.48 to 3.83) and the history weights are positive, but no reading meets all parts. On the code's sessions with reading (a), the 50% weight kept for the 7 of 70 mice shown 50% trials in the basic task, the four history weights are within tolerance (0.2021, 0.4299, 0.2974, 0.4404) but the mean visual weights do not increase with contrast; with reading (b), 50% trials dropped, they increase and the basic unrewarded weight is 0.2966, just below 0.297. With the code's P1b, a variant, the sessions of reading (b) meet all parts under both 50% readings, as does the pipeline's contrast check on the code's sessions with reading (b). The answer on P1b (first full-task session at or after P1) confirms the sessions used; the answer on the 50% weight names the two readings run, and both give partial. The failure to increase under reading (a) is not an effect of averaging the 50% weight over 7 mice and the others over 70; over the 7 mice with every weight the means for 6.25% to 100% are 0.93, 1.55, 2.35, 8.05 and 3.25. Earlier outcome the same (partially_reproduced). Measured is the code's sessions, reading (a).

outcomes.statement: Previous choices influenced behavior more strongly in the full task than in the basic task, after both rewarded and unrewarded trials.
outcomes.source: Results, A probabilistic model reveals common strategies across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 5d,g
outcomes.quote: Indeed, previous choices more strongly influenced behavior in the full task, both after rewarded (t(125) = 10.736, p<10 −6 ) and unrewarded trials (t(125) = 4.817, p<10 −6 ).

statistics.about: rewarded past-choice weight, full against basic
unrewarded past-choice weight, full against basic

outcomes.notes: On the code's sessions both weights are larger in the full task under every reading and both 50% readings (main, rewarded t = 9.91 and 9.94, unrewarded t = 3.54 and 3.56, p < 0.001; all readings, rewarded t = 8.91 to 10.69, unrewarded 3.54 to 3.79). On the sessions of reading (b) the unrewarded difference is not significant (p = 0.10 to 0.39). The criterion takes its weights from fig5cf-glm-weights, whose sessions are the code's with (b) a reading of the Methods, and which allows a match under one reading; the code's sessions match here. The answers changed P1 and named the 50% readings, which agree; earlier outcome the same (reproduced). The verifier's round 1 gave partially_reproduced (see verifications).

outcomes.statement: The model predicted individual mouse choices well, with cross-validated accuracy of 81.03 +- 5.1% in the basic task and 82.1 +- 5.8% in the full task, similar across laboratories; mean condition numbers were 2.4 and 3.2.
outcomes.source: Results, A probabilistic model reveals common strategies across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 5, figure supplement 2c
outcomes.quote: Importantly, fitted weights and the model's predictive accuracy (unbiased: 81.03 + 5.1%, biased 82.1 + 5.8%) ( Figure 5—figure supplement 2 ) were similar across laboratories, suggesting an overall common strategy.
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading, on the code's sessions, the legend's accuracy is 81.9% (basic) and 83.5% (full), within tolerance, and the full-task condition number 3.14 is within 3.2 +- 0.32. The basic-task condition number is 2.38 under reading (b), 50% trials dropped (within 2.4 +- 0.24), and 2.89 under reading (a), the 50% weight kept for the 7 mice shown 50% trials (outside). The criterion takes the fits of fig5cf-glm-weights and allows a match under one reading, and all four values are within tolerance under reading (b). The code's accuracy reading gives 74.3% and 76.4%, also within tolerance; accuracy varies by less than 0.1% over fold seeds. The revision before round 1 had blocked the claim under the notebook's own rule that readings of an open detail must agree, which the criterion does not state; the verifier's round 1 gave reproduced, and the rule is dropped. Measured is the code's sessions, reading (b).
deviations: The cross-validation seed is a standard choice (0), with seeds 0 to 4 shown.

outcomes.statement: Fitted model weights and predictive accuracy were similar across laboratories.
outcomes.source: Results, A probabilistic model reveals common strategies across mice and laboratories, paragraph 2; Figure 5, figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: The model fit the mouse choices well and captured the relative importance of sensory and non-sensory information across mice and laboratories
outcomes.notes: Under the main reading 6 (code's sessions) and 7 (sessions of reading (b)) of the 19 lab tests give p < 0.05, under both 50% readings, mostly visual weights (6.25% contrast in both tasks, p = 0.001 to 0.046); the criterion allows two for partial. With the code's P1b, a variant, 2 and 4 tests do; under the other variants 2 to 8. The answers changed P1 and P1b and added reading (a) to the tests; earlier outcome the same (not_reproduced).

outcomes.statement: After correcting for slow fluctuations in decision bound, most mice used a win-stay lose-switch strategy, in both the basic and full tasks.
outcomes.source: Figure 5, figure supplement 1b legend; Results, A probabilistic model reveals common strategies across mice and laboratories, paragraph 3
outcomes.quote: When taking these slow state-changes into account, the majority of animals use a win-stay lose-switch strategy.
outcomes.notes: More than half the mice have both a positive corrected post-reward shift and a negative corrected post-error shift, in each task (main, basic 0.587 of 63 mice, full 0.859 of 71; code P1b, 0.596 and 0.833). The answers changed P1 and P1b; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).
deviations: "More than half the mice have a positive ... and a negative ..." is read as mice with both; the fractions for each alone are shown (0.71 to 0.97).
Run under the main reading of P1, with both readings of P1b, to keep the notebook within its time limit.

outcomes.statement: After rewarded trials, choice updating was largest when the previous stimulus had low contrast and much smaller after high-contrast rewarded trials.
outcomes.source: Figure 5, figure supplement 1c legend
outcomes.quote: After rewarded trials, choice updating is largest when the visual stimulus was highly uncertain (i.e. had low contrast) but strongly diminished after more certain, rewarded trials.
outcomes.notes: After rewarded trials, mean corrected updating after 0% and after 6.25% contrast exceeds that after 100% in both tasks (main, full task 11.35 and 8.44 against 6.73%; basic 15.48 and 10.87 against 5.13%), and with the code's P1b. In the basic task the 0% value rests on 4 mice; with 0% and 6.25% pooled the result is the same. The answers changed P1 and P1b; earlier outcome the same (reproduced).
deviations: Run under the main reading of P1, with both readings of P1b, as for fig5s1b-win-stay-lose-switch.

outcomes.statement: The session-ending criterion was not mandatory; 5,316 of 10,903 sessions ended earlier and 5,587 later, the latter continuing for a median of 19 +- 16 extra trials (m.a.d.).
outcomes.source: Results, Training progression in the basic task, paragraph 2; Figure 1, figure supplement 2
outcomes.quote: The criterion to end a session was not mandatory: some sessions were ended earlier (5,316/10,903 sessions) and others ended later (5,587/10,903 sessions). The latter sessions typically continued for an extra 19 ± 16 trials (median ±m.a.d., 5,587 sessions) longer.
outcomes.notes: The project mice have 6,539 sessions (against 10,903). 5,698 met an end criterion and 841 ended earlier (13%, against 5,316 of 10,903, 49%). Extra trials median 16.0, m.a.d. 14.0, against 19 +- 1.9 and 16 +- 1.6. Only the count of sessions meeting a criterion is within tolerance, while the share differs. Per training day, counting a day as met when a session met a criterion or the day's sessions lasted 90 minutes or more, 5,683 of 6,435 days met one. The criterion defines the count per training day, but the outcome is decided on the per-session count; the outcome is the same either way. Recomputing the criteria also for the 722 sessions whose status is False, a variant, gives 5,734 of 6,539 (88%), with the same extra trials. Not affected by the answers.
deviations: The end status is the rig setting SUBJECT_DISENGAGED_TRIGGERED with its trial number, taken as the pipeline's SessionEndCriteriaImplemented; for the 486 sessions without it the criteria of the legend are recomputed, and a status of False counts as not met (recomputed in a variant).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds 178 mice and 6,615 sessions from 2019-06-11 to 2020-03-23. The paper's mice began training in January 2019 (206 mice, 10,903 sessions), so 41 mice of the project begin mid-training in the dandiset and the mice trained before June 2019 are missing.

The training status of each session (in_training, trained_1a, trained_1b, ready4ephysrig and so on), on which every analysis of the paper selects sessions, is not in the files. It has to be recomputed from the trials, which leaves open details of the criteria.
One recording is deposited twice, under two mice (CSHL_013 and CSHL_015, 2019-07-15, identical trials and start time).

probabilityLeft is described as the probability of a left stimulus for the current block, but in every basic-task session it varies from trial to trial between 0 and 1 (24% of basic-task trials are not 0.5), with the stimulus side following it.
session_start_time is stated in UTC (+00:00) but holds local clock times; all seven labs, from London to Berkeley, have median start hours between 11.0 and 14.4 h.

In 807 files the wheel position data and its timestamps differ in length (for example 181,623 samples against 340,799 timestamps); 16 files have no wheel series. In one session checked (ibl_witten_07), the wheel moves the opposite way to the choice on every trial.

257,021 trials (6%) have no stimulus onset time, and 185 sessions have none; 1,541 trials in 220 sessions have a response time before the stimulus onset (down to -5,638 s). No proficiency window of this attempt fails for the missing onsets alone.
One session (ZM_1367, 2019-06-11) uses contrasts of 4% and 8%, which the paper does not describe.

The Methods give the 1a/1b performance criterion on easy trials and the Results give the lapse criterion as a maximum of 0.2 for the sum of the lapses, while Appendix 1, table 1d gives performance on 100% contrast and a bound on each lapse rate. After the answers of 2026-10-22 the claims file follows the pipeline's code for performance (easy trials) and the table for the lapses; with performance on 100% contrast only, 84 mice reach P1 against 83.
The dandiset's metadata do not say which of its 178 mice are the paper's; one mouse (SWC_029) belongs to another project by its subject record.

disagreements.reason: Cell 16: Kruskal-Wallis p=0.029, so the labs differ at 0.05 but not at the required <0.001. Lab 2 IQR 7.75 is in tolerance; Lab 6 IQR 5.75 is far from 22.

Cell 73: Logistic Regression is not above chance (2.5th percentile 0.000 vs 0.070). Cell 75: Random Forest ran only 6 of the 2000 subsamples; those 6 are not above chance, but that decides nothing. It also noted (problem 4) that the Random Forest needs about 4.9 h single-threaded on data already loaded, a block that is not a data limit, and asked for the full 2000-subsample run in parallel.
Cell 51: 91 mice vs 150+-15. Trials per session differs (FDR p=0.002) as claimed, but trials per minute also differs (FDR p=0.002). Cell 73: the classifier is not above chance.

Cell 84: accuracy (81.9 / 83.5) and full-model condition number 3.14 are in tolerance under every reading. entries.name: 000045-ibl-2021
entries.title: Standardized and reproducible decision-making in mice (The International Brain Laboratory 2021)
entries.description: Tests the findings of The International Brain Laboratory (2021) on dandiset 000045, which holds the trial tables of 178 mice trained in seven laboratories from June 2019 to March 2020. It recomputes basic and full task proficiency from the trials and compares training times, psychometric parameters, block effects, the choice model and session ends with the paper, across laboratories. The dandiset holds no sessions before June 2019 and no training status.

notebooks.title: Reproducing The International Brain Laboratory (2021) from dandiset 000045
